I want to give a bit of a rundown for people who are new to this of my understanding of how things are going.

  1. First off you need to understand how the Hugo awards work. Most awards have a committee that selects books and chooses a winner. The committee is usually full of great people in the world of books who aren't authors (or at least not primarily authors). You get publishers, agents, directors of literacy foundations, etc to form your committee and select books. They then select a number of other people like them to select a winner. So you get a bunch of book people choosing a great book. Not the Hugo. The Hugo is chosen by people who have attended a Sci Fi con in the last 3 years. It's a specific con, but if you go you get to vote on books nominated. It's part of the reason the Hugo award (if you've read many Hugo winners) can be really hit or miss in my opinion. It also means that it's easy to manipulate votes...after all you don't need THAT many people on your side, and all you have to do is buy a ticket to get a vote.

  2. So what happened? Well about a year and a half ago someone blogging on TOR.com wrote about post-binary gender in sci fi. He bemoaned the lack of non traditionally gendered people in modern sci fi and basically caused for more cause oriented books to be written and published. Larry Correia responded. He was harsh on the content of the blog and basically said that readers want a story and that causes are boring. A really great writer can put story first and still have the cause in there, but putting cause first just makes books that won't sell. These two blog posts as far as I can tell are basically what started the whole thing off.

  3. Once side decided to basically put in a fix on the Hugo awards and nominate what thought belonged. In fact the list of nominations was pretty much exactly the same as a list on a Rapid Puppies blog.

  4. An editor at TOR said

There are two extreme right-wing to neo-nazi groups, called the Sad Puppies and Rabid Puppies respectively, that are calling for the end of social justice in science fiction and fantasy. They are unrepentantly racist, misogynist, and homophobic. A noisy few but they’ve been able to gather some Gamergate folks around them and elect a slate of bad-to-reprehensible works on this year’s Hugo ballot. 5. People decided to boycott TOR who wouldn't say anything against her.

My opinion is basically that you have the SJW crowd pitted against a mix of authors who are concerned about their genre and red-pills. Honestly the Hugo has been about as suspect of a major award as ever there was and this just undermines it further. I agree with the Sad Puppies that if you put cause before story you write a shit book, but I'm also apprehensive of a push back that says these causes aren't important. I think it's important to note that I DO NOT think that the authors themselves are saying the causes are not important, but I DO think that a lot of their support is derived from groups that really do NOT like these issues. Anyway, I'll continue to read books that look good no matter who wrote them or published them and I'll take my Hugo winners with more salt than I used to.
